title: Canonical compact-support coefficient comparison and normalized open coordinates
statement:
Let $A,B$ be finite commutative unital rings and $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital ring homomorphism. For schemes use the ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and scalar extension $T_T^{A,B}=(-)\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. All geometric pullbacks, direct images, and adjunctions are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with canonical constant-ring comparisons. For a scheme map $q:T\to V$, define $R q_{*,A}$ by that normalized derived direct image, the canonical tensor/pullback isomorphism $q_B^*T_V^{A,B}\simeq T_T^{A,B}q_A^*$ by the balanced K-flat tensor map, and $\gamma_q:T_V^{A,B}Rq_{*,A}\to Rq_{*,B}T_T^{A,B}$ as its mate: its transpose is $T_T^{A,B}(\varepsilon^A)$ after that pullback isomorphism.

For each $q$ and $A$, let $e_q:q_{\mathrm{tensor}}^*\simeq q_{\mathrm{intrinsic}}^*$ be the unique ordinary module-pullback isomorphism preserving the sectionwise units: for every module $F$, object $W$ of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and $s\in F(W)$, $e_{q,F}(\eta^{\mathrm{tensor}}_F(s))=\eta^{\mathrm{intrinsic}}_F(s)$ as sections over $T\times_V W$. This unique isomorphism exists; it identifies the two presentations of pullback, without choosing an arbitrary natural isomorphism.

For an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$, let $j_!^A$ be the sectionwise sheafified extension by zero of [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Also use its normalized left-adjoint presentation $J_j^A\dashv j_A^*$. Define the ordinary comparison of these left adjoints by uniqueness after identifying their right adjoints through $e_j$, and descend it termwise to $r_j^A:j_!^A\simeq J_j^A$. Define $\beta_j:T_Z^{A,B}J_j^A\simeq J_j^BT_X^{A,B}$ as the unique comparison of composite left adjoints whose right-adjoint comparison is the canonical scalar-restriction/pullback identification. Define $e_j^{A,B}:T_Z^{A,B}j_!^A\simeq j_!^BT_X^{A,B}$ by transporting $\beta_j$ through $r_j^A,r_j^B$. For any $p:Z\to Y$, define $F_{j,p,A}=Rp_{*,A}j_!^A$ and the natural transformation $b_{j,p}^{A,B}:T_Y^{A,B}F_{j,p,A}\to F_{j,p,B}T_X^{A,B}$ by $b(M)=Rp_{*,B}(e_j^{A,B}(M))\circ\gamma_p(j_!^AM)$. These are actual functors and natural comparisons on the entire ambient categories; properness of $p$, boundedness, constructibility and finite Tor amplitude are not required to define them.
